Michigan sentiment miss plus sticky inflation expectations keeps the no-Fed-pivot overhang on the tape.

S&P 500 +0.4%, Nasdaq +0.6%, Dow +0.4%, Russell 2000 +0.2% in late-morning trade; Nasdaq on pace for a 4th straight weekly gain. Roundhill Mag7 ETF +~1% with every Mag7 name green except AAPL. WTI ~$91.50 (flat late-morning after dipping ~1.2% to $90.40 overnight); Brent ~$102.91. BTC ~$83,000.

headlines.headline: Indexes rebound in late-morning trade: S&P 500 +0.4%, Nasdaq +0.6%, Dow +0.4%, Russell 2000 +0.2%; Nasdaq on pace for a 4th straight weekly gain and the Roundhill Mag7 ETF is +~1% with all Mag7 names green except AAPL.
headlines.why_it_matters: Dip-buying after Thursday's OpenAI-revenue selloff is broadening - the tape is voting that the AI-capex cycle, not the revenue-measurement dispute, is the story.

headlines.headline: Michigan consumer sentiment (preliminary October) fell to 46.3 from 48.1 in September, below the 48.0 expected - a third straight monthly decline, near the record-low 44.8 from May. One-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% (from 4.6%) and five-year to 3.5% (from 3.4%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Weak sentiment plus rising inflation expectations is the worst combo for a hawkish Fed - it argues against any pivot to cuts, keeping the 5%+ yield headwind in place.

headlines.headline: UBS analyst David Vogt says iPhone 18 Pro wait times compressed ~6 days week-over-week, an 'increasing concern' with stable supply; Neutral, $296 price target. Jefferies and Bernstein also flagged soft demand. AAPL fell ~2.1-2.5% to ~$333 in morning trade. Possible offset: the iPhone Duo foldable launches Oct 23 ($1,999, preorders Oct 16), so some 18 Pro buyers may be waiting.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second independent demand read amplifies Nikkei's report of a 15-20% October component-order cut - hardware revenue is at risk, though the foldable launch genuinely muddies the signal.

headlines.headline: NVDA rebounded ~1.5% early (recovering about half of Thursday's -2.9%), then faded to roughly flat ($229.96) - choppy. Fresh negative wrinkle: Australian data-center firm Firmus Grid scrapped a $5B IPO at a $30B valuation (3x its $10.5B two months ago); Nvidia is an investor and Firmus rents chips to OpenAI and Meta. Calming factor: analysts say the $50B-vs-$70B revenue gap is a measurement discrepancy - Anthropic counts cloud-partner sales from AWS/Google Cloud, OpenAI doesn't. OpenAI still has not responded to the FT.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound shows AI-spend conviction returning, but Firmus keeps valuation-risk headlines alive - the revenue-measurement confusion is the noise layer on top of real demand.

headlines.headline: American Express fell 1.4-1.7% after the OCC and Fed fined it $350M over anti-money-laundering failures covering ~$13B of suspicious activity from 2014-2025. Consent orders include no asset cap; AXP says it had already reserved for the fine and kept 2026/2027 guidance unchanged.
headlines.why_it_matters: Headline overhang but no capital or growth constraint - the muted price reaction says the market treats this as a known, contained cost.

headlines.headline: SpaceX-spectrum rotation continued this morning: SPCX +3% (bouncing from two days of losses) while VZ -6%, T -7%, TMUS -9% on satellite-carrier competition fears; tower names CCI/SBAC/AMT +6-12%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is pricing Starlink Mobile as a real fourth national carrier - carriers get re-rated down while towers win either way.

headlines.headline: Oil eased further on de-escalation rhetoric: Trump said on Truth Social Thursday there are 'productive discussions' with Iran and no attack before the Nov 3 midterms, with the blockade staying; Iran's FM says Tehran is reviewing the US response to a proposal to reopen Hormuz within 7 days. Fresh US sanctions Thursday (individuals, networks, 17 vessels) and Hurricane Isaias (1.3M bpd, 62.9% of Gulf production shut in) keep a floor under crude. WTI ~$91.50 flat late-morning after dipping ~1.2% overnight; Brent ~$102.91.
headlines.why_it_matters: De-escalation rhetoric eases the wartime supply premium, but sanctions plus hurricane shut-ins keep the floor - airlines and refiners still live with elevated crude.

headlines.headline: Delta's Q3 EPS $1.72 vs $1.77 expected; revenue $17.6B vs $17.7B expected; the carrier slashed its 2026 profit outlook, blaming Iran-war-driven jet fuel costs. Stock -2% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Confirms the fuel-cost squeeze is an airline-sector theme, not Delta-specific - watch United and American for the same damage.

headlines.headline: Humana +12% (IBD 10:15 AM ET), clearing the 419.97 buy point after CMS raised Medicare Advantage star ratings - 18 contracts scored at least four stars.
headlines.why_it_matters: Star ratings directly lift future MA revenue - a sustained quality repricing, not a one-day bounce.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried forward: Oct 1 8-K - issued 34.47M Class A units at $26.7206 (fixed 9.25% distribution, non-convertible, non-redeemable, unlisted) to J-W Energy in an internal reorg; began TXSE listing Oct 5 under USAC; Q2 2026 beat Aug 4 ($0.31 EPS vs $0.28 est, $342.15M revenue vs $340.49M est); $600M 6.75% notes due 2035 issued in September to repay credit facility debt; next earnings est 11/04/2026; consensus Hold with $29.50 target.

Whether the Iran-Hormuz negotiation progress materializes or oil re-prices higher again

iPhone Duo foldable launch Oct 23 ($1,999) - the demand wildcard for the AAPL read
10Y yield pressing toward 5.30%+ multi-decade highs - every rally has to climb over it
analysis: The morning's clearest new data is Michigan sentiment (46.3, third straight decline, inflation expectations up), which lands on the side of the Fed hawks - Waller and Musalem get no help pivoting dovish, so the 10Y keeps grinding (+4bp to 5.27% today). Meanwhile equities are shrugging it off: the S&P +0.4% and Nasdaq +0.6% rebound is a conviction vote that Thursday's AI selloff was a one-day multiple-compression event. The most useful development in the OpenAI story is not price action but the measurement explanation - Anthropic's figures include cloud-partner revenue, OpenAI's don't, which shrinks the 'miss' into an accounting dispute rather than a demand break. But two unconfirmed threads still hang over the tape: no official OpenAI response, and the Nikkei Apple cut report (now seconded by UBS's wait-time read, though the foldable launch is a real confound). The SpaceX rotation is the session's purest signal: one credible entrant headline took 6-9% off every major carrier while towers ran 6-12% - competitive-moat repricing, not earnings. Net: a relief morning with a sentiment-economics undercurrent that could cap how far this rebound runs.

community_signals.title: The headline should've been 'OpenAI annualised revenues $20B less than previously...'
community_signals.takeaway: Comment thread reframes the FT story: the $40B/$70B figures came from OpenAI's own investors 'grossing up' OpenAI's numbers for a direct Anthropic comparison (Anthropic counts cloud-partner sales; OpenAI doesn't), then applying 70%+ growth to the inflated baseline - so the 'miss' is a correction of a flawed extrapolated consensus, not a revenue collapse. Direct counter-analysis the headlines barely carried.
